meta.topStoryHeadline: 79th Tony Awards: Joshua Henry Wins Best Actor, Qween Jean Makes History as First Trans Tony Winner
meta.topStorySummary: Joshua Henry won Best Actor in a Musical for Ragtime at Lincoln Center Theater, and Qween Jean — born in Haiti, founder of Black Trans Liberation — became the first openly transgender person to win a Tony Award for her costume design on Cats: The Jellicle Ball. Ragtime also won Best Revival of a Musical. Both productions center Black and Afro-diasporic cultural traditions.
executiveSummary: The 79th Tony Awards delivered historic wins for Black artists: Joshua Henry won Best Actor for Ragtime, Qween Jean became the first openly transgender Tony winner for Cats: The Jellicle Ball — a production built around ballroom and voguing culture.

The Obama Presidential Center opens on Juneteenth in Chicago — 30 commissioned works by 30 Black artists, 23 accessible free outdoors. The largest collection of site-specific Black artist commissions at any single institution in recent American history.

Juneteenth week is the richest cultural week of the year in New York. June 19 alone holds five free events: Seneca Village at 1 PM, Ogemdi Ude at Prospect Park at 6 PM, Okwui Okpokwasili on Governors Island at 6 PM, Oh Sankofa! at Lincoln Center at 7 PM, and the Unsung Collective at Bryant Park at 7 PM.

events.title: Step Afrika!: The Migration — Reflections on Jacob Lawrence
events.dates: Through June 21 · 7:30 PM · Also Carnegie Hall June 17
events.description: The world's leading stepping company transforms Jacob Lawrence's 60-panel Migration Series into a full-evening work of percussive dance, live gospel, jazz, and blues. Joyce Theater debut. Also Carnegie Hall June 17.

events.title: Met Opera Summer Recital — Lonwabo Mose
events.description: Free outdoor recital featuring South African bass-baritone Lonwabo Mose alongside Met Opera colleagues. Works by American composers. First-come, first-served.

events.title: Studio Museum Artist-in-Residence Open Studios
events.description: Rare studio access to three emerging Black and Afro-Latinx artists — Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, and Taylor Simmons — in the Museum's new building. First Open Studios in the new space.

events.title: Schomburg Centennial Festival — Literary Programming
events.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
events.description: Centennial-year literary festival with author talks, book workshops, panels, and a Toni Cade Bambara film talkback. One of Harlem's most important literary days of the year.

events.title: Met Opera Summer Recital — Joshua Blue
events.venue: SummerStage Central Park · Brooklyn Bridge Park
events.dates: Mon, June 15 (Central Park) · Wed, June 17 (Brooklyn Bridge Park)
events.description: African American tenor Joshua Blue performs free outdoor recitals at two locations this week. Works by American composers.

events.title: Bronx Museum Juneteenth Celebration 2026
events.description: Juneteenth evening celebration at the Bronx Museum with galleries open late. The Seventh AIM Biennial: Forms of Connection on view.

events.title: Seneca Village Juneteenth Performance
events.address: W 85th St at West Drive, Central Park
events.description: Site-specific performance at the exact location of Seneca Village — the Black community that thrived from 1825 until the city seized it to build Central Park in 1857. Music, dance, spoken word, and history on the ground where it happened.

events.title: Studio Museum in Harlem: Juneteenth Community Day
events.description: Extended hours and community programming alongside Fade and Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED on Juneteenth.

events.title: Ogemdi Ude: MAJOR — Juneteenth Performance
events.description: Danspace Project and Prospect Park present Ude's rigorous, kinetic work on majorette dance culture. With Bria Bacon, Kris Lee, and AJ Wilmore. Co-presented by Danspace Project and Prospect Park Alliance.

events.title: Okwui Okpokwasili / Sweat Variant: my tongue is a blade
events.description: Three-hour movement performance by one of the most important Black women in experimental performance in the United States. Free on Governors Island over Juneteenth weekend.

events.title: Oh Sankofa! A Juneteenth Celebration — Lincoln Center
events.venue: Hearst Plaza and Damrosch Park, Lincoln Center
events.description: Evening-length Juneteenth celebration curated by Carl Hancock Rux. Chanon Judson of Urban Bush Women, Marvin Sewell, and the Etienne Lashley Choir. Dance, live music, choral performance, and storytelling.

events.title: The Unsung Collective: Juneteenth Concert — Bryant Park
events.address: Bryant Park, 42nd St and 6th Ave, Manhattan
events.description: Harlem's chamber orchestra marks Juneteenth with a program dedicated entirely to Black American composers: Jessie Montgomery's Starburst and Five Freedom Songs, and works by H. Leslie Adams.

events.title: Calvin Royal III in Swan Lake — ABT
events.description: Soirée Founding Ambassador Calvin Royal III performs Prince Siegfried in American Ballet Theatre's Swan Lake at the Metropolitan Opera House. Christine Shevchenko as Odette/Odile.

events.title: Yinka Esi Graves: The Disappearing Act
events.dates: Sat, June 20 · 7:30 PM · Sun, June 21 · 4:00 PM
events.description: New York premiere of a solo performance illuminating flamenco's African roots and Afro-descendant contributions to Andalusian culture. Born in London to a family from Ghana and Jamaica. Part of the inaugural Lincoln Center Contemporary Dance Festival.

events.title: 651 ARTS: We Outside! A Brooklyn Juneteenth, Vol. IV
events.description: 651 ARTS transforms the Downtown Brooklyn plaza into a free all-day arts and performance gathering. Artwork by Jocelyn Goode. Live performances, a marketplace by Black artisans, and a community cypher.

events.title: Calvin Royal III in Onegin — ABT
events.description: Soirée Founding Ambassador Calvin Royal III performs Lensky in John Cranko's Onegin at the Metropolitan Opera House.

events.title: Calvin Royal III in Onegin — ABT
events.description: Soirée Founding Ambassador Calvin Royal III performs Lensky in John Cranko's Onegin at the Metropolitan Opera House.

events.title: ABTKids — Hosted by Misty Copeland
events.description: One-hour family introduction to ballet, hosted by Misty Copeland and ABT dancers.

events.title: Studio Museum: Museums as Systems Symposium
events.description: Annual symposium on museum practice. This year's theme: Black study. For members interested in the intellectual and institutional dimensions of the arts.

events.title: Romeo and Juliet — Free Shakespeare in the Park
events.description: Directed by Saheem Ali, with Tony winner LaChanze and Hamilton's Okieriete Onaodowan. Free outdoor Shakespeare. Final weeks.

events.title: Joe Turner's Come and Gone — Broadway
events.description: August Wilson's portrait of the Great Migration, directed by Debbie Allen, with Taraji P. Henson's Broadway debut. The must-see Broadway production of the season.

events.title: Ragtime — Broadway
events.description: Tony Award-winning revival (4 Tonys including Best Revival and Best Actor). Joshua Henry plays Coalhouse Walker Jr. in this masterwork about race, dignity, and injustice in early 20th-century America.

events.title: Cats: The Jellicle Ball — Broadway
events.description: Tony Award-winning production reimagining the classic through Black and Latinx ballroom and voguing culture. Qween Jean's historic costume design — first openly transgender Tony winner. Three Tony Awards. Extended through January 2027.

news.title: 79th Tony Awards: Joshua Henry Wins Best Actor, Qween Jean Makes History as First Trans Tony Winner
news.summary: Joshua Henry won Best Actor in a Musical for Ragtime at Lincoln Center Theater — the production's first Tony after four prior nominations. Qween Jean, born in Haiti and founder of Black Trans Liberation, became the first openly transgender person to win a Tony Award for her costume design on Cats: The Jellicle Ball. Ragtime also won Best Revival of a Musical.

news.title: Obama Presidential Center Opens on Juneteenth with Landmark Collection of Black Artist Commissions
news.discipline: Visual Art · Public Art · Cultural Institution
news.summary: The Obama Presidential Center in Chicago's Jackson Park opens to the public June 19 on Juneteenth. 30 commissioned works by 30 Black artists — Njideka Akunyili Crosby, Theaster Gates, Lorna Simpson, Rashid Johnson, Carrie Mae Weems, Mark Bradford, Julie Mehretu, and others. 23 works accessible outdoors, free of charge. The largest collection of site-specific commissions by Black artists at a single institution in recent memory.

news.title: Dallas Black Dance Theatre Names First Executive Director After Labor Dispute That Saw Entire Company Fired
news.summary: DBDT has named Kristie Patton Foster executive director, following a 2024–25 labor dispute in which the company fired its entire main company after dancers unionized with AGMA. The dispute cost DBDT $560,000 in NLRB settlements. The company approaches its 50th season.

news.title: 2026 Guggenheim Fellows Include American Artist, Sonya Clark, Allison Janae Hamilton, and Kyle Abraham
news.summary: The 2026 Guggenheim Fellowship class includes Black artists American Artist (conceptual/tech-based work), Sonya Clark (textile, hair), Allison Janae Hamilton (interdisciplinary), and choreographer Kyle Abraham, founder of A.I.M by Kyle Abraham in its 20th year.

news.title: Federal Judge Rules NEH Grant Terminations Unconstitutional — DOGE Used ChatGPT to Flag 'History,' 'Culture,' 'Identity'
news.summary: Judge Colleen McMahon permanently barred the Trump administration from canceling over $100 million in NEH grants, ruling the process unlawful and unconstitutional. DOGE admitted using ChatGPT to flag grants containing 'history,' 'culture,' and 'identity' as DEI-related. The FY2027 White House budget still proposes eliminating IMLS entirely.

news.title: Black Arts Organizations Lose NEA and IMLS Grants — Challenge America Program Cancelled
news.summary: The NEA's Challenge America program — which for over 20 years funded small arts organizations serving underserved communities — has been cancelled for FY2026. Museum Hue lost both an NEA matching grant and an IMLS National Leadership Grant. Research on the systemic underfunding of culturally-specific institutions has been interrupted.

news.title: Cave Canem Marks 30th Anniversary — Exhibition Opens at August Wilson Cultural Center
news.summary: Cave Canem — the foundational organization for Black poets in the United States — marks 30 years in 2026 with a Fellows reunion this month and a satellite exhibition 'the total black, being spoken' opening at the August Wilson African American Cultural Center, running through June 2027.

news.title: Colson Whitehead Completes the Harlem Trilogy — Cool Machine Publishes July 21
news.summary: Cool Machine, Whitehead's tenth novel and the conclusion of the Harlem Trilogy, publishes July 21. Set in 1981 New York, bringing Ray Carney's saga into the era of reckless real estate and corruption. Publishers Weekly calls it 'the greatest New York novel in years.' From a two-time Pulitzer Prize winner.

news.title: Photography and the Black Arts Movement, 1955–1985 Travels to Mississippi Museum of Art July 25
news.summary: The first exhibition to center photography's role in the Black Arts Movement travels to the Mississippi Museum of Art July 25, after runs at the National Gallery of Art and the Getty. Co-curated by Deborah Willis.

appointments.name: Kristie Patton Foster
appointments.role: Executive Director, Dallas Black Dance Theatre
appointments.description: First executive director at DBDT following a significant labor dispute. 20 years of nonprofit leadership. Company approaches its 50th season.

appointments.name: Lisa Brown Ross
appointments.role: President & CEO, African American Museum of Dallas
appointments.description: Effective July 21, 2026. Leadership at one of the country's dedicated African American museums.

appointments.name: Lynda Roscoe Hartigan
appointments.description: Takes the SAAM director role September 8, 2026. Previously developed SAAM's collection of American folk art and African American art.

appointments.name: Lisa Funderburke
appointments.role: Director & CEO, Newark Museum of Art
appointments.description: One of the few Black directors at a mainstream US art museum. Howard University alumna.

appointments.name: Alicia Graf Mack
appointments.role: Artistic Director, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater
appointments.description: Only the fourth person to hold this role in 67 years. The position is now endowed at $10 million.

appointments.name: Koyo Kouoh
appointments.description: First African woman selected to curate the Venice Biennale. Her vision — 'In Minor Keys' — being realized by her team through November 2026.

exhibitions.title: 2026 Artists in Residence: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, Taylor Simmons
exhibitions.description: Three emerging Black and Afro-Latinx artists in residence. Culminating exhibition opens September.

exhibitions.title: Fade — 17 Emerging Artists of African and Afro-Latinx Descent
exhibitions.description: The sixth 'F' show of emerging artists. Seventeen artists across painting, sculpture, video, and installation.

exhibitions.title: Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED
exhibitions.description: Site-specific commission drawing on the 'flying geese' quilting pattern — a symbol of the Underground Railroad — in fugitive dyes that shift over time.

exhibitions.title: The Seventh AIM Biennial: Forms of Connection
exhibitions.description: Emerging NYC-based artists from underrepresented communities. Closes June 29 — free.

exhibitions.title: Ideas of Africa: Portraiture and Political Imagination
exhibitions.description: MoMA's survey of African and African diasporic photography — Malick Sidibé, Kwame Brathwaite, Seydou Keïta, Njideka Akunyili Crosby, and others. Curated by Oluremi C. Onabanjo. Closes July 25.

exhibitions.title: Whitney Biennial 2026
exhibitions.description: The 82nd edition, curated by Marcela Guerrero and Drew Sawyer. Includes Precious Okoyomon and artists of African descent.

exhibitions.title: Venice Biennale 2026: In Minor Keys — Koyo Kouoh (Posthumous)
exhibitions.description: First African woman to curate the Venice Biennale. Her vision realized by her team after her passing in May 2025.
